ov: The hybrid of a male tiger and a lioness. It can have both spots from its mother and stripes from its father, and males grow at most a short, ruff-like mane. Unlike the liger it grows no bigger than its parents. Tigons exist only in captivity.

why.dg: As big as its parents, lions and tigers, and both of those kill people.

rg: Only in captivity, because lion and tiger habitats do not overlap in the wild today.

cf.tip: A tigon has a tiger father and a lion mother; a liger is the reverse cross and grows much bigger, often 320–550 kg.

fx: Male tigons are sterile, but females can breed: a tigoness at India's Alipore Zoo had seven cubs with a lion.
One of those cubs, a "litigon" named Cubanacan, weighed at least 363 kg.
